# Engine 13.4.0 release notes, mined and iterated to the cut

Terminal predicate: Engine 13.4.0 is published by `publish.mjs` with release notes a reader can follow: named chapters on what the release delivered, every claim anchored to its primary, and the counts regenerated at the cut head.

## Problem

13.4 is the householding release (`ROADMAP.md`, *Next: Engine 13.4*). The operator moved its cut to this weekend, Saturday 2026-11-07 in the evening or Sunday at the latest, and set the gate at fewer than 25 open Engine issues (#20465). `publish.mjs` refuses to cut without `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/v13.4.0.md`. At 2026-11-06T22:30Z no notes file, branch, ticket or claim existed, and `package.json` on `dev` still reads 13.3.1.

The window since 13.3.1 (published 2026-10-23T23:27:07Z) is not small. The release-notes §2 count over the `github-content-sync` corpus (head `443b7e4`, 2026-11-06T20:55Z) finds 251 merged PRs, 307 closed issues and 15 closed epics. The headline is not one feature. In the same window:
- the open backlog fell from 103 toward the gate in a day of premise reads (#15000);
- Engine CI started running each test tier only where a change can reach it (#20328);
- the single-app Neural Link specs left the Bridge (#20370);
- feature and fix work landed across grid, form, data and components;
- outside contributors landed their PRs.

"Householding" names the gate. It must not shrink the story (release-notes §1, rule 4).

**Why an epic, not one ticket.** The release-notes protocol makes notes multi-iteration by design. Iteration 1 merges early behind its banner. Mining leaves refine the chapters. The final iteration (banner off, numbers at the cut head, designations confirmed) gates `publish.mjs prepare`. Each of these is a one-PR leaf, linked here as sub-issues.

## Intended solution

- **The staging note** `.github/RELEASE_NOTES/v13.4.0.md` is iterated on `dev` under `.agents/skills/release-notes` (§1–§7). The bar is the precedent set. Each cut's `dropReleasedNotes` removes older notes from `.github/RELEASE_NOTES`, so the set is read from GitHub Releases: 13.3.0 (the latest minor), 12.1.0, 11.24.0, 11.23.0 and 11.22.0. A minor carries one or more named chapters, not a changelog. Its Full Changelog tail comes last and is regenerated at the cut.
- **Scope from the corpus** (§2): `buildScripts/release/analyzeClosedSinceRelease.mjs <cutoff> --corpus-root <github-content-sync>/neo`, re-run against live GitHub at the cut head.
- **Chapters from Memory Core mining per arc** (§3). An arc without mining behind it is a candidate, not a chapter.
- **Every claim anchored** (§4). `Release Type` and `Stability` are the operator's to confirm, never inferred.
- **The cut** is one leaf of mechanics here plus the cut record, filed once the notes near §7: version bump, `publish.mjs prepare --rehearse` → `prepare` → `finish`, npm and Portal read-backs. The cut's one human step is merging the release PR.

## Out of scope

- The under-25 householding itself (#15000 and its stewards). The notes report it; they do not drive it.
- The post-release roadmap section (`/update-roadmap`).
- The Brain and Institution release lines (`ROADMAP.md`'s line table).

## Avoided traps

- **A changelog dump with a title on top.** Grouped tables support the story; they never replace it (§5).
- **A single-pass PR.** The v13.1 first draft shipped environment errors and one-lens narration (§1).
- **Counting from the engine's own content mirror.** It no longer exists (#19159); the corpus is the only source.
